title: Police identify shootout victim: Man who died in Highway 401 gunfight lay on the side of the road, handcuffed, for 12 hours
article: The man killed in a shootout with police on Highway 401 has been identified as Daniel Lamer, 37, of Montreal, and his associate has been identified as a former member of the Rockers biker gang.
The Rockers are a puppet club used as bodyguards and enforcers for the Quebec Hells Angels' elite Nomads chapter.
Mr. Lamer's associate, Marc Bouffard, was being recruited to eventually become a full-fledged Hells Angel and had been recently transferred to Ontario to look after some of the bikers' activities.
The Nomads are the most violent chapter in the Hells Angels criminal organization.

Mr. Bouffard, 27, was allegedly behind the wheel of a red Pontiac Sunfire when shots were fired at Ontario Provincial Police Const. Dan Brisson Sunday morning during a routine traffic stop just west of the Upper Canada Road exit, near Morrisburg.

He and Mr. Lamer were westbound on Highway 401 about five kilometres west of Morrisburg when Const. Brisson stopped the vehicle for speeding. The officer radioed for help when the two men had difficulty understanding the officer, who spoke only English.
Two other officers arrived and parked behind the stopped car before "all hell broke loose," according to one officer.

Const. Brisson was hit by a shot that ricocheted off his bulletproof vest and grazed the back of his head. At least one of the officers then fired back, killing Mr. Lamer who had been seated in the front passenger seat.
It's unclear whether Mr. Lamer was inside the car when he was shot, but the officers handcuffed the body on the side of the road.

Officers arrested Mr. Bouffard and yesterday afternoon he made a brief appearance in a Cornwall courtroom to face charges of attempting to escape officers, fraudulently impersonating a man by the name of Eric Martin and misleading an officer on his identity. More serious charges are expected at a later date.
Four police officers stood guard inside the courtroom as Mr. Bouffard appeared, only to be remanded in custody to April 2.
Mr. Bouffard did not speak during the appearance and wore glasses, a white shirt and blue jeans.
Mr. Lamer's body was taken to Ottawa Hospital General campus for an autopsy yesterday.
Investigators from Ontario's Special Investigation Unit arrived on the scene at 1:30 p.m. and began an investigation into the shooting.
Mr. Lamer's body lay on the side of the road, handcuffed, uncovered and in full view of eastbound traffic, for almost 12 hours while investigators tried to piece together what happened.
The investigators are trying to find out if the police officer was within his rights to draw his gun and open fire.
SIU spokeswoman Rose Hong said it was regrettable that passing motorists saw Mr. Lamer's body, and she didn't know why it was left uncovered.
"It's something we'll investigate," she said. "But there's a variety of reasons it would remain uncovered. These decisions are made at the scene."
Police finally cleared the scene and opened the highway around midnight.
The Rockers, formed in 1992, manage the Hells Angels drug network in Montreal. Below them, the main puppet club controls three street gangs.
Const. Brisson, meanwhile, spent yesterday at his Cornwall home with family, including his wife and five-month-old daughter.
Const. Brisson was born and raised in Cornwall before joining the Metro Toronto Police Service.
He spent two years there before transferring to the OPP to get closer to his hometown. He has been stationed with the Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry detachment since November.
The two other officers who answered the call for backup are both longtime veterans of the OPP, each with more than 10 years service.
"All we are doing is making sure the officers have all the support and assistance," said Sgt. Ed Kinnear, vice-president of the Ontario Provincial Police Association.

OPP officers and 10 investigators assigned to the case have yet to complete their interviews. Two OPP officers have been assigned to work specifically with witnesses. Ms. Hong would not comment on the specifics of the investigation.
